regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: Create the missing off-body near-wake box so the separated-shear-layer / bluff-body wake envelope is covered. Bounds are the flow_requirement:near_wake envelope padded by ~0.01 m so the float32 bounds (0.3499999940/1.0499999821/+-0.9799999833/+-0.4899999917) are strictly contained. Level 2 gives 0.04375 m, half the 0.0875 m prior (= exactly level 1), leaving a factor-2 margin for the native p95 span statistic (tolerance 1.5) instead of a knife-edge equality. Level 2 stays coarser than surface level 3, so no surface/layer/quality setting changes and the surface -> wake -> background grading is preserved. Volume 0.72*1.98*1.00 = 1.43 m^3, ~1.7e4 cells. This is an envelope prior, not a measured shear-layer thickness.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Cover the downstream velocity-deficit/shear transport envelope, padded ~0.01-0.02 m beyond the float32 bounds (1.0499999821/2.4499999583/+-1.2599999785/+-0.6299999893). The prior span 0.175 m is EXACTLY the uniform background cell (grading 1.0), so leaving it unboxed relies on an equality that any stricter native comparison or transition cell would break; level 1 = 0.0875 m supplies a factor-2 margin at ~6.9e3 cells. The upstream face overlaps the near-wake box by 0.02 m so maximum level wins and no coarse slot appears between the two envelopes. Kept deliberately at one increment (the scenario states coarser far-wake bounds cost), not refined to surface level.

advisor.hypothesis: The failure is a boundary-layer extrusion/coverage defect localized to the two streamwise END CAPS (|Y| ≈ 0.70), not resolution and not angle clamping. Measured evidence: the cap slab query [-0.36,-0.71,-0.36]..[0.36,-0.69,0.36] returns coverage_5plus = 0.0 with area_fraction 0 layers = 1.0 over 0.424 m² of wall area — a FULLY unextruded planar disc. The mirror slab gives coverage_5plus 0.5485 with 14.6% at zero layers. The native mechanism log confirms this is a squeeze-collapse, not an angle suppression: "Extruding 10578 out of 12069 faces (87.646%)" with 0 removed faces, and directional_outward_hit_distance finite_fraction = 0.0 at both caps and over the whole body — the outward normal-ray cohort finds no finite fluid gap, i.e. no wall-adjacent clearance is resolved there. The layer_shortfall:0 cluster (2048 pts, wall distance ~5.7e-17, measured_local_full_feature 1.40 m) sits at x/z = ±0.393 and |Y| 0.603–0.744, i.e. the cap rim ring. Requested stack 0.00653 m against a global surface cell of 0.021875 m at level 3 means the first cell size exceeds the whole requested layer stack, so the shrinker cannot pack 5 layers in the available clearance and deletes them (the "Disabled extrusion" / isolated-region-removal path); the 0.021875 m surface cannot even resolve the 0.001 m first height. Counterevidence for prior mechanisms: round 2 raised layer feature_angle 60→120 (angle hypothesis) and coverage fell 0.840→0.682; rounds 1 and 3 applied local_refine level 4 at the rim and coverage stayed 0.84/0.757 while adding ~70–80k cells and raising max_skew to 2.8–3.3. With fraction_adjacent_edges_above_layer_feature_angle = 0.0 at the caps (dihedral p50 45°, p95 90°), the 90° crease is below the configured 120° layer angle, so feature_angle is NOT the binding mechanism. The remaining causal lever per version reference: surface_level and the layer stack must be co-designed, and normal/thickness smoothing plus a medial rotation allowance must free displacement at the crease. Plan: (1) surface_level 3→4 so the free surface cell (0.0109375 m) is comparable to the requested 0.00653 m stack — the only way 5 real layers can physically fit; (2) layer_settings restoring the measured-good round-0/1 expansion 1.2 with feature_angle 60 (proven 0.80–0.84, better than 120), max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.6 to allow the full stack in the concave rim, min_medial_axis_angle 60, and raised thickness/normal smoothing; (3) removal of the now-passive repair_0 level-4 box (it inflates cost and skew at the rim while the resolution fix is global); (4) modest snap smoothing so the finer snapped crease does not fold. No wake box is touched.
advisor.expected_change: Primary measurable target: area_fraction_by_layers[0] at the cap slabs falls from 1.0 (mirror slab 0.146) to below 0.10 and the body-wide coverage_5plus rises from 0.7565 toward ≥0.90, with the native "Extruding X out of 12069 faces" fraction rising from 87.65% toward ≥95%. Secondary: max_skew should not exceed the observed 3.28 and the quality gate (max_non_ortho 65, check skew 4.0) must still pass; the native self-intersection check must move from unavailable/failed to passing as the creep-fill is removed by the coarser-wake/finer-surface transition. Cost: surface_level 4 raises surface and near-body cells roughly 2-4x over the current 237824 (well within the 2e6 budget), partly offset by removing the repair_0 level-4 box. Uncertainty: the 0.41/0.42 m² caps contributing ~13.7% of area must fall below 10% zero-layer to pass; if the shrinker still deletes layers because the true fluid clearance at the planar cap is smaller than the 0.00653 m stack, coverage will stay below 0.90 and a further first-height/stack reduction (not a geometry change) would be the next distinct lever. This is a meshing-probe expectation only; separation, wake recovery and wall y+ remain unvalidated until a solver run.
alternatives: Keep surface_level 3 and instead drop the requested stack (n_surface_layers 5 with expansion_ratio 1.05) so the stack 0.0056 m even more exceeds the 0.021875 m surface cell — rejected: the surface cell remains 4x the whole stack, so the cap faces still cannot host 5 cells.

Switch mesh_shrinker to displacementMotionSolver (v2412 reference: smoother Laplacian shrinking, lower induced velocity) — plausible as the next distinct intervention if the medial-axis mover still deletes cap layers; not chosen first because the measured defect is geometric clearance/cell-size mismatch, which a different mover does not create.
Add n_grow 2 to make the cap transition safer — rejected: nGrow propagates NON-EXTRUSION and would lower, not raise, cap coverage.
Restore plan:f89da707d10e40d8 (round 0, 0.797) — not eligible_for_restore; all four catalog entries are marked ineligible, so the anchor settings are adopted as the baseline by value instead.
Further local_refine at the rim — already tried in rounds 1 and 3 with no coverage gain, so repeating it without a new causal reason is excluded.

actions.why: repair_0 is a level-4 volume box sitting exactly on the cap rim deficit. Rounds 1 and 3 showed it does not create layer space (round 1: 0.840 coverage with the box; round 3: 0.757 with the box) but it does inflate cells to 237824 and max_skew to 3.28. The resolution repair is now global via surface_level, so the box is redundant cost and a skew source at the crease. Removing it does not touch flow_near_wake/flow_far_wake, so both flow_requirement native coverages stay 1.0.
actions.name: repair_0

actions.why: Root cause measured as cell-size/stack mismatch: requested layer stack is 0.00653 m while the level-3 global surface cell is 0.021875 m, i.e. a single surface cell is 3.3x the ENTIRE requested stack. The cap slab query shows the consequence: coverage_5plus = 0.0 with 100% of 0.424 m2 of cap wall area at zero layers, and the native log shows only 10578/12069 faces (87.65%) extruded. Raising global surface_level 3->4 gives a free surface cell of 0.0109375 m, comparable to the 0.00653 m stack, so five real cells can be packed on the cap and rim. base_cells is left at 8 so the far-field background cell and hence the already-accepted near/far-wake native p95 spans are unchanged.

Restore the measured-BEST layer baseline by value (round 0/1: expansion_ratio 1.2, feature_angle 60, n_surface_layers 8/7 gave coverage 0.797/0.840) and reject round 2's angle hypothesis (feature_angle 120 drove coverage 0.840->0.682). At the caps fraction_adjacent_edges_above_layer_feature_angle is measured 0.0 with dihedral p95 90 deg, so 60 deg already exceeds the crease angle: feature_angle is not binding and a wide angle only harms the smooth barrel. max_thickness_to_medial_ratio is raised 0.3->0.6 and min_medial_axis_angle lowered 90->60 so the medial-axis mover accepts the full requested stack in the concave cap rim instead of halving thickness toward minThickness; n_smooth_thickness 30, n_smooth_normals 15, n_smooth_surface_normals 8 and n_relax_iter 15 redistribute the rim displacement instead of collapsing it; max_face_thickness_ratio 0.6 re-enables the warped-face extrusion guard. n_grow stays 0 (it propagates NON-EXTRUSION and would lower coverage), n_buffer_cells_no_extrude stays 0, n_outer_iter stays 1 (it partitions layers, it is not a retry). Absolute first height 0.0010702 m is unchanged, so the flat-plate target-y+ 50 planning estimate is preserved.

The finer level-4 crease at the cap rim is the same location as the snap_artifact and transition clusters (concaveFaces:1/2/3 at |Y| 0.46-0.55, wall distance 0.0231 m; concaveCells:9 with 1149 cells at 0.0699 m) and the failed boundary native self-intersection evidence. Raising n_smooth_patch 6->10, n_relax_iter 8->15 and n_feature_snap_iter 20->30 while keeping the snap explicit (implicit false) smooths the snapped rim surface and reduces fold/creep risk that the medial mover converts into disabled extrusion. tolerance is kept at 2.0 so no additional insertion scale change is introduced, and no quality gate is loosened.
